lines.text: P01, Brandlhuber. We closed in seven rounds at one hundred thirty-four euros eighty per unit, from April 2027 instead of November. That is fifty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-four euros below their opening offer, a score of zero point nine three. All three arguments in round one were verified by the foundry: quality record, volume change and notice period. About four thousand two hundred euros stayed on the table. Ask me why, or what I would change.
Where did we leave that money?
Round three. The foundry came down about four thousand two hundred euros, and we gave sixteen thousand two hundred in a single step, almost four times their move.
In round four we pulled back thirteen and a half thousand. The owner called it a step backwards, and one round later he sent his final offer.

Never out-concede the supplier. In the planner, I would cap our step at zero point eight times their last step, down from one point one, so we never have to take an offer back. I have sent it to Agent Studio for your approval.

params.title: Never out-concede the supplier
params.rationale: P01 round 3: the foundry moved €4,235, we moved €16,190 (3.8×). In round 4 we pulled back €13,496; the owner called it "a significant step backwards" and sent a final offer one round later.
